## 固定收益核心論點

7月28日美國公債連續第3個交易日收高，更重要的是，漲勢結構轉佳。2年期與5年期殖利率均下跌5個基點，分別收在4.26%與4.35%；10年期下跌4個基點至4.61%，30年期則回落3個基點至5.09%。7月27日油價下跌雖壓低損益兩平通膨率，10年期實質殖利率卻仍走高；本次實質殖利率也加入跌勢，10年期實質殖利率下跌3個基點至2.41%，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅下滑1個基點至2.20%。油價回跌開始減輕實質折現率負擔，不再只是壓低通膨補償。

油價仍是利率方向的主要驅動因素。美國與伊朗出現降溫跡象後，布蘭特原油創下2020年以來最大3日跌幅；繼前一週一度升破每桶100美元後，週二再跌1.62%至86.93美元。這波走勢削弱Fed因能源衝擊立即採取行動的理據，讓政策敏感型美國公債領漲。2s10s曲線陡化1個基點至35個基點，2s30s陡化2個基點至83個基點，部分扭轉先前通膨衝擊造成的曲線趨平。

不過，這波漲勢並未消除政策機制轉變帶來的不確定性。儘管按兵不動仍是較可能的結果，交換市場定價7月29日升息25個基點的機率仍約為3分之1。8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量週一增至967,136口，突破歷史紀錄，顯示風險高度集中於單次會議。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh降低對前瞻指引的依賴，使不確定性本身成為固定收益定價因素：油價下跌削弱立即緊縮的經濟理據，卻未能恢復市場對Fed會認可其偏好利率路徑的信心。

信用債與股票另有保留訊號。存續期間較長的信用債基金隨美國公債走高，但費城半導體指數下跌4.49%；中國競爭、資本支出能否持續，以及超過7,500億美元的Nvidia相關AI融資安排，加深市場對科技融資風險最終由誰承擔的疑慮。S&P 500仍上漲0.21%，VIX下跌2.46%，高收益債基金也溫和走高。這不是全面避險，而是資金撤出高槓桿投資主題，整體融資環境仍正常運作。

全球存續期間壓力也使美國公債漲勢不能直接解讀為全面寬鬆。歐洲投資人持續定價更高的政策利率與結構性較陡的長端；日本同時承受財政與匯率壓力；台灣殖利率曲線也因本地流動性與利率預期而大幅重定價。新興市場美元債受惠於美國公債殖利率下跌與美元持平，但各國主權債表現仍取決於財政可信度與債務管理選擇。因此，本次收盤確實反映美國實質利率環境改善，但異常集中的Fed事件風險、持續的長端供給競爭，以及信用市場更嚴格的個別定價，仍限制利多。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

美國公債有序上漲，漲幅集中於前端。2年期與5年期殖利率各下跌5個基點，超過10年期的4個基點與30年期的3個基點。這種走勢反映油價回落後，市場下修近期政策溢價，而非放棄財政供給與通膨不確定性所要求的長期補償。牛市趨陡幅度有限，2s10s為35個基點、2s30s為83個基點，但已扭轉前一交易日的牛市趨平，也顯示當日利多較集中於預期政策路徑。

拉長觀察期間，金融情勢仍偏緊。與1個月前相比，2年期殖利率高19個基點，5年期與10年期均高23個基點，30年期則高22個基點。殖利率月線近乎平行上移，顯示近期油價回跌尚未抹去各期限要求報酬率的普遍升幅。即使美國公債已連漲3個交易日，30年期殖利率仍達5.09%，反映沉重的財政與期限溢價門檻。因此，單日曲線陡化應解讀為高殖利率環境下的事件風險緩解。

通膨連結定價呈現相較7月27日最關鍵的變化。10年期名目殖利率下跌4個基點，其中實質殖利率下跌3個基點，損益兩平通膨率下跌1個基點。前一交易日名目殖利率下跌，則來自損益兩平通膨率下滑5個基點，實質殖利率反而上升1個基點。週二實質殖利率為2.41%，仍較1個月前高23個基點；但單日回落顯示，投資人下修政策不確定性與存續期間所需的實質補償，不再只把油價下跌視為整體通膨的機械式調整。

商品價格支持實質殖利率回落，但通膨背景尚未完全正常化。布蘭特原油收在86.93美元，1週下跌4.48%；WTI收在82.24美元，同期下跌3.14%。兩者較1個月前仍約上漲19%至21%。外交進展降低供應再度中斷的機率，近期能源衝擊因而減弱；但月線累計漲幅意味企業與政策制定者面對的燃料及運輸成本仍高於衝突升級前。這股拉扯解釋了為何週二實質殖利率明顯回落，損益兩平通膨率卻僅小幅下降。

Fed定價對油價下跌反應有限。紐約時間下午3時30分，交換市場顯示隔日決策升息25個基點的機率約為3分之1；市場仍完全定價9月前升息25個基點，並定價明年3月前升息近50個基點。多數經濟學家預期利率不變，但Citadel Securities已把基本情境改為升息，PGIM也認為市場低估升息機率。預期分布很寬，因為爭點不只在政策利率，也在Warsh是否會以未事先預告的行動，建立更難預測的反應函數。

期貨部位讓事件溢價清楚可見。8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量由週五909,714口增至週一967,136口，超越2024年10月合約創下的原紀錄。部位增加主要鎖定眼前按兵不動或升息的二元結果，選擇權部位也集中於2026年稍後到期的SOFR履約價。透過美國公債期貨防範長債拋售的成本，仍高於防範長債上漲的成本；即使現貨殖利率下跌，投資人仍把長存續期間資產損失視為代價更高的尾端風險。

前瞻指引減少，會提高兩次會議之間所需的風險補償。Warsh已成立工作小組檢討Fed溝通方式，並質疑央行反覆暗示可能政策路徑的做法。這種方式長期或可減少虛假的精確度，但在7月29日前，市場也失去原本能讓預期決策與最終結果維持在數個基點內的定錨。自2015年以來，會議前一日的平均誤差僅2.4個基點；本次會議卻隱含約8個基點的預期緊縮，明顯偏離近年操作慣例。

因此，殖利率曲線傳達的訊號，比3日漲勢所暗示的更有限。油價下跌帶動實質殖利率回落與小幅牛市趨陡，顯示能源衝擊已不再透過所有利率管道收緊金融情勢。然而，整條曲線較1個月前上移、30年期殖利率高於5%，加上長端拋售避險成本偏高，結構性負擔仍在。週二壓低了近期通膨尾端風險的定價，卻未釐清Fed利率路徑或財政期限溢價能否持續下降。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用債隨美國公債上漲，但違約風險並未大幅重定價。LQD上漲0.30%，HYG上漲0.19%，JNK上漲0.16%。投資級債漲幅較大，符合其存續期間曝險較高的特性；2檔高收益債基金漲幅相近，也顯示半導體股遭到拋售之際，風險偏好仍具韌性。不過，過去1個月LQD仍下跌2.44%，HYG與JNK則分別下跌0.51%與0.63%。整體市場的主要拖累仍是高實質殖利率，而非廣泛信用壓力。

Meta相關資料中心融資顯示，大幅新券讓利可以吸引次級市場需求。BlackRock發行125億美元債券，殖利率為7.53%，利差較美國公債高287.5個基點。訂單最高達200億美元，僅為發行規模的1.6倍，遠低於2026年美國投資級債發行約4倍的平均水準。承銷耗時近1週，最終條件未較初步討論收窄，最終利差也是3年來A級以上債券最寬水準。這些條件顯示，承接瓶頸在價格，而非市場已經關閉。

次級市場表現改善了市場評價，但沒有抹去初始訊號。高殖利率吸引買盤後，利差週二收窄至約267個基點。Meta是德州1吉瓦設施初期的唯一承租戶，設施預計2028年開始營運；BlackRock旗下基金持有合資事業80%，Meta持有20%。租約初始期限為4年，另有4次續約選擇權；若設施公允價值低於預先約定門檻，剩餘價值保證將彌補部分差額。即使租約與資產價值支持安排明確，投資人仍要求高額補償。

AI信用風險也正透過保證與客戶融資移轉，不再只經由傳統債券發行。投資人評估超過7,500億美元的基礎設施安排之際，Nvidia違約保障成本創下活躍交易以來最大升幅。中國在浸潤式深紫外光微影技術取得進展，也增添營運威脅，意味已融資產能的定價能力可能轉弱。信用分析的問題已不只是科技業將發行多少債務，而是AI使用率若不如預期，哪些企業資產負債表將承擔租賃、採購與剩餘價值義務。

傳統併購融資仍可取得，條件也明顯較單純。Brady私募發行8億美元投資級債務，為14億美元收購Honeywell生產力解決方案事業的交易籌資。債券期限介於5年至10年，其中規模最大的3億美元7年期券，定價較可比美國公債高125個基點。Brady另有一筆10億美元定期貸款，由多家貸款機構組成銀團。這筆交易顯示，能穩定產生現金流的成熟資產仍可透過多種管道融資，成本僅為Sopaipilla利差的一小部分，普通併購槓桿與AI專案集中風險之間仍有明確區隔。

Tullow Oil則顯示，商品價格帶來的額外收入如何重啟原本受阻的再融資管道。該公司4月展延約12億美元債券，以4.23億美元票據替換Glencore的4億美元貸款，並新增貨物預付款融資，之後開始評估2027年以較低成本舉債。重整後債券交易價格接近面額的102%，受現金流改善，以及4月一批貨物以每桶130美元成交所支撐。不過，除非公司在2027年9月30日前簽署出售協議，觸發式提前到期條款將使還款日提前6個月，因此執行成效仍同時取決於營運進展與油價。

未評等市政債市場則更積極地把營運風險轉移給投資人。QCF/I計畫發行約6.1億美元、分別於2046年與2057年到期的債券，為收購Advantage Behavioral Health籌資，行銷利差約較可比AAA債高300個基點。其中約4.15億美元將支付給Clearview Capital與公司內部人士，另有1億美元取決於績效。這項事業的價值中，僅1,440萬美元來自自有不動產，因此債券持有人主要承擔預估營運現金流風險，而非由實體資產提供保障。另有約30億美元同類融資案正在籌備，使此案的先例意義不限於單一交易。

歐洲銀行資本面臨相反問題：充裕需求在損失事件發生前，已把補償壓得很低。多幣別AT1指數利差收窄至211.3個基點的歷史低點，2家銀行發行的優先證券也創下最低重設利差。收益仍具吸引力，但Man Group認為，投資人低估銀行債務結構最次順位部分的展延、不付息與本金損失風險。美國軟體業再融資則提供另一項規模測試。Veritas支持的Gainwell正討論替換近$57億債務，包括約$42億第一順位與$15億第二順位貸款；整體軟體業在2028年前約有$920億槓桿貸款到期。債券與貸款方案可以延長優先債務，既有貸方則可能保留次順位部分，因此交易能否完成，同時檢驗市場容量與多少風險仍由原債權人承擔。信用流動性仍正常運作，但市場區隔相當明顯。美國公債上漲支撐總報酬，Meta相關債券在次級市場獲得買盤，Brady也透過私募債與銀行貸款完成併購融資。若還款仰賴長期AI使用、或有保證、商品價格復甦或進取的營運預測，市場就要求高出許多的補償；AT1利差收窄則顯示，其他複雜風險獲得的補償異常偏低。週二沒有出現融資停擺，而是反映結構性保障、資產品質與讓利，已比籠統的風險偏好升溫更具分析分量。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

油價下跌雖帶來短期喘息，歐洲存續期間資產仍有結構性陡化傾向。歐元10s30s交換利差連續第3個交易日走陡，但仍接近10個基點；2月衝突已抹去先前走勢約60%。隨財政發債增加、荷蘭把1.6兆歐元退休金制度轉為確定提撥制，投資人仍預期短天期債券表現優於長端。市場定價歐洲央行年底前升息42個基點。前端仍受能源與政策牽制，長端則面臨穩定買盤逐步流失。

日本則透過財政可信度與匯率承受同一股拉扯。有報導指出，首相高市早苗可能指示官員規劃把食品消費稅降至1%，為期2年，引發市場對融資與日本公債增發的疑慮。日圓維持在1美元兌163日圓以上的弱勢區間；市場預期日本央行可能加快緊縮以抑制輸入性通膨，帶動短端殖利率上升、曲線趨平。財政寬鬆威脅長端，較快的政策路徑則壓迫前端，也降低日本買方持有海外存續期間資產的相對吸引力。

市場定價反映兩項壓力難以同時化解。隔夜交換市場定價日本央行9月前升息的機率約29%，10月前為78%，但50%的受訪經濟學家預期下一次行動要到12月。1%的政策利率仍遠低於官員討論的約2%中性利率。台灣也印證區域利率正在重定價：20年期公債標售需求疲弱，加上市場預期未來12個月至少升息1次、幅度12.5個基點，使5年期殖利率跳升16個基點至1.82%，創2008年11月以來新高。

美國收盤後，智利央行連續第5次會議把政策利率維持在4.5%，決策一致通過。布蘭特原油前一週一度升破100美元，週二盤中又跌破85美元，使這個燃料幾乎全數仰賴進口的經濟體通膨預期劇烈震盪。油價下跌仍不足以重啟降息：6月通膨率已升至4.3%，高於3%目標，投資、消費與就業指標則轉弱。這項決策反映更普遍的全球限制，現貨能源價格下降雖可降低政策急迫性，卻無法消除累積的物價壓力。

稍後公布的英國財政評估，顯示長存續期間資產還面臨另一項競爭來源。英國國家經濟社會研究院估計，本屆國會任期內，通膨與能源成本可能侵蝕240億英鎊公共服務支出的實質購買力，並使財政規則緩衝空間減少約30億英鎊。該院預測2026年與2027年平均通膨率均為3.1%，高於國際貨幣基金與經濟合作暨發展組織預測的2.4%平均值，也接近英國央行3%的中間情境。該院預期政策利率維持3.75%，市場則定價至少升息2次至4.25%，雙方對通膨路徑的分歧足以左右市場。

英國買方已開始因應這項不確定性。多資產基金雖提高整體債券配置，但12月至6月間，gilt占固定收益配置的比重由25%降至15%，資金轉向Germany、Japan、Australia、New Zealand與Canada。這批資金規模小於專門投資gilt的基金，但仍顯示，當通膨與國內政治風險降低投資信心時，高名目殖利率本身不足以留住買方。NIESR則量化財政面的影響：能源、通膨與借款成本上升，可能在本屆國會任期內侵蝕£240億公共服務預算，並減少約£30億財政規則緩衝；其預測2026年與2027年平均通膨均為3.1%。NIESR預期BOE把利率維持在3.75%，低於市場定價的4.25%，因為再舉債填補缺口只會惡化已不可持續的債務路徑。對美國公債而言，即使美國殖利率下跌，全球資金對存續期間資產的競爭仍在。歐洲退休金改革與財政供給支撐長端曲線走陡；日本減稅計畫與日圓疲弱，讓政策與發債承受方向相反的壓力；台灣則顯示，本地流動性一旦收縮，原本的低殖利率市場可能迅速重定價。智利與英國也證明，油價回落不會自動重啟寬鬆空間。因此，海外主權債殖利率與各國融資需求，將繼續限制買方對美國利率下降的反應。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場美元債受惠於美國公債上漲，但沒有明顯匯率助力。EMB上漲0.24%，長存續期間新興市場美元主權債指數也上漲0.24%，美元指數則僅下滑0.04%至101.43。新興市場貨幣收盤大致持平，油價下跌有利進口國，商品出口國則承受相反的貿易條件衝擊。新興市場股票下跌3.7%，主要由亞洲科技股拖累，而非美元普遍短缺。美國公債實質殖利率下降，降低共同的融資門檻，但各地資產負債表仍決定個別結果。

阿拉伯聯合大公國發債顯示，市場在直接地緣政治壓力下仍具韌性。截至7月28日，主權國家與企業透過美元及歐元債券籌得303億美元，較一年前增加33%，也比歷年同期紀錄高37億美元。近期發行包括RAK Bank的6億美元、Burjeel的5億美元，以及Ajman的3億美元伊斯蘭債券；多數發行超額認購，最終條件也較初始指引收窄。阿拉伯聯合大公國主權美元債利差仍較美國公債高約77個基點，寬於戰前的65個基點，顯示市場准入與較高的衝突溢價可以並存。

不過，不同債務管理策略取得的市場准入並不一致。哥倫比亞審計長質疑一項10月債券交換；政府以面額43.4兆哥倫比亞披索的TES，交換面額35.4兆哥倫比亞披索的新券，使名目債務減少約8兆哥倫比亞披索並延長到期日。新券票面利率為11.75%與12%，高於原券約7.25%，使每年利息支出增加約3,165億哥倫比亞披索。財政部主張，較低票面利率將迫使政府提供更深折價、發行更多名目債務；但案件移送紀律審查後，未來負債管理也增加法律與制度風險。

哥倫比亞案例的意義不只在會計爭議，也在於區分短期流動性紓解與跨期財政能力。2025年基本赤字占GDP 3.5%，債券交換原本就在較弱的財政背景下進行。以高成本長債替換短期工具雖降低再融資壓力，卻也讓未來政府承擔更高償債支出，壓縮其他支出空間。對主權債投資人而言，若票息負擔與治理程序同時改變，就不能把到期日延長視為毫無保留的改善。

其他市場的初級發行准入仍具選擇性。烏拉圭著手增發2035年到期的本幣債與2037年到期的美元債，整體新興市場貨幣指數消化油價跌勢後則幾乎沒有淨變動。油價衝擊重新分配金融情勢，而非使各地一致收緊：智利等進口國獲得匯率紓壓，能源相關借款人則失去近期部分收入助力。美元穩定與美國實質殖利率下降改善外部環境，卻都無法抵銷財政執行、商品敏感度，以及債務管理決策能否經得起法律檢驗的影響。

新興市場的共同因子帶來喘息，但主權債分化仍在。硬通貨存續期間資產上漲，波斯灣發行人仍可進入市場，也未出現廣泛的美元流動性斷裂。阿拉伯聯合大公國利差走寬與哥倫比亞具爭議的債券交換，則標示風險所在：即使訂單簿穩健，市場仍會計入地緣政治曝險；到期結構管理也會按完整的未來成本評價。美國公債漲勢改善了折現率，卻沒有讓各國主權信用趨於一致。

## 跨資產

跨資產走勢確認油價是利率上漲行情的起點，但不支持經濟全面衰退或資產清算的解讀。布蘭特原油下跌1.62%至86.93美元，WTI下跌0.45%至82.24美元，延續局勢降溫後的跌勢，並壓低美國公債名目與實質殖利率。S&P 500仍上漲0.21%，等權重指數更創新高，防禦型與非科技類股抵銷昔日AI領漲股的弱勢。VIX下跌2.46%至18.21。殖利率下降與整體股票維持韌性並不矛盾。

壓力集中於科技業。Nasdaq 100下跌0.98%，費城半導體指數重挫4.49%，後者1週與1個月跌幅分別達10.69%與16.42%。投資人同時評估中國產能風險與AI循環融資疑慮，亞洲半導體股也大幅下挫。這種分化支持信用面的解讀：市場質疑的是資本密集產業的報酬與義務結構，而非定價全體經濟現金流崩跌。

美元與黃金進一步削弱避險解讀。美國公債上漲之際，美元指數仍近乎持平，黃金期貨反而下跌1.25%至4,023.40美元。信用債基金與新興市場債也同步走高。整體走勢顯示，能源通膨降溫與實質利率壓力減輕，是主要的寬鬆傳導管道，科技業特定壓力則與之並存。這不像資金不分標的追求流動性，也不是全面撤出信用風險。

## 前瞻市場意涵

7月29日FOMC決策將決定事件風險消退後，實質殖利率能否維持跌勢。若升息25個基點，或按兵不動但仍把近期緊縮列為積極選項，壓力將集中於2年期殖利率、聯邦基金期貨，以及中期美國公債的實質利率部分。若Fed耐心按兵不動，並更加重視油價下跌與6月通膨降溫，上述指標就必須延續漲勢，而不能再靠損益兩平通膨率下滑。7月31日公布的就業成本指數，接著將檢驗能源衝擊減弱後，薪資壓力是否仍支持Fed殘存的通膨疑慮。若布蘭特原油再度漲向前一週高點，兩條傳導管道都會重啟，週二的牛市趨陡也將證明只是暫時現象。

Microsoft與Meta將於7月29日公布財報，Apple與Amazon則於7月30日接續公布，為AI信用提供現金流與義務檢驗。若收入相對已揭露的資本承諾仍具韌性、新增保證有限，且Sopaipilla利差守在週二267個基點附近或以內，就能維持原有解讀：7.53%的殖利率雖是大幅讓利，仍有效促成市場成交。若支出增加卻沒有相應現金流、客戶融資承諾進一步增加，或Nvidia違約保障再度轉弱，疑慮將從半導體股擴及高評級企業資產負債表。敏感傳導管道包括長天期科技債、後續訂單簿，以及仰賴租約與剩餘價值支持的專案融資結構定價。

英國央行7月30日決策與日本央行7月31日決策，將檢驗海外曲線能否減輕與美國公債競爭的壓力。若英國央行指引確認市場定價的升息至4.25%路徑，英國公債的通膨與財政溢價將進一步提高；若展望更接近英國國家經濟社會研究院以3.75%為中心的看法，殖利率就必須下降、通膨預期也須轉穩，才能讓此一展望取得可信度。日本方面，若指引把升息時點由12月提前，就必須穩定日圓且不能再引發前端拋售；鴿派訊息則可能使日圓貶破1美元兌165日圓，再度引發干預疑慮。對美國公債的最終影響，取決於這些結果會壓低海外主權債殖利率、改善避險後的美國存續期間資產需求，或使各國本地資產繼續爭取全球資產負債表配置。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The July 28 Treasury close extended the rally to a 3rd session and, more importantly, improved its composition. The 2-year and 5-year yields each fell 5 basis points to 4.26% and 4.35%, the 10-year declined 4 basis points to 4.61%, and the 30-year eased 3 basis points to 5.09%. Unlike July 27, when lower oil compressed breakevens but the 10-year real yield still rose, real yields participated: the 10-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.41% as the 10-year breakeven slipped only 1 basis point to 2.20%. The energy-risk reversal began to ease the real discount-rate burden rather than merely remove inflation compensation.

Oil remained the dominant catalyst for the direction of rates. Brent's worst 3-day decline since 2020 followed signs of de-escalation between the US and Iran, and the contract fell another 1.62% to $86.93 after trading above $100 during the prior week. That path weakened the immediate case for an energy-driven Fed response and allowed the policy-sensitive Treasury sector to lead. The 2s10s curve steepened 1 basis point to 35 and 2s30s steepened 2 basis points to 83, reversing part of the flattening associated with the earlier inflation shock.

The rally did not resolve the policy regime change. Swaps still assigned roughly a 1-in-3 chance to a 25-basis-point increase at the July 29 decision, despite a hold remaining the more likely outcome. August federal funds futures open interest reached 967,136 contracts on Monday after breaking the prior record, showing how much risk was concentrated around a single meeting. Chairman Kevin Warsh's reduced reliance on forward guidance made the uncertainty itself a fixed-income input: lower oil reduced the economic case for immediate tightening, but it did not restore confidence that the Fed would validate the market's preferred path.

Credit and equities imposed a separate qualification. Duration-sensitive credit funds rose with Treasuries, yet the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.49% as Chinese competition, capital-spending sustainability and more than $750 billion of Nvidia-linked AI arrangements sharpened concern about where technology funding risk ultimately sits. The S&P 500 still gained 0.21%, the VIX fell 2.46%, and high-yield funds advanced modestly. This was not a generalized flight to safety. It was a rotation away from a highly leveraged investment theme while broad financing conditions remained functional.

Global duration also prevented the US rally from becoming an unqualified easing signal. European investors continued to price higher policy rates and a structurally steeper long end, Japan faced simultaneous fiscal and currency pressure, and Taiwan's curve repriced sharply around local liquidity and rate expectations. Emerging-market dollar debt benefited from lower Treasury yields and a flat dollar, but sovereign outcomes remained governed by fiscal credibility and debt-management choices. The close therefore marked a genuine improvement in US real-rate conditions, bounded by unusually wide Fed-event risk, persistent long-end supply competition and a more discriminating credit market.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The Treasury rally was orderly but front-loaded. The 5-basis-point declines in the 2-year and 5-year sectors exceeded the 4-basis-point move in the 10-year and the 3-basis-point decline in the 30-year. That sequence fits a market reducing the immediate policy premium as oil retreated, rather than one abandoning the long-run compensation required for fiscal supply and inflation uncertainty. The resulting bull-steepening was modest, with 2s10s at 35 basis points and 2s30s at 83, but it reversed the prior close's bull-flattening and located the day's relief closer to the expected policy path.

The longer horizon remains restrictive. Compared with 1 month earlier, the 2-year yield was 19 basis points higher, the 5-year and 10-year were each 23 basis points higher, and the 30-year was 22 basis points higher. The near-parallel monthly increase shows that the recent oil reversal has not erased the broader rise in required returns across maturities. At 5.09%, the long bond still embeds a substantial fiscal and term-premium hurdle even after 3 sessions of gains. The daily steepening is therefore best understood as event-risk relief within an elevated yield regime.

Inflation-linked pricing supplied the most important change from July 27. The 10-year nominal yield's 4-basis-point decline combined a 3-basis-point fall in the real yield with a 1-basis-point fall in breakeven inflation. On the prior close, the nominal rally had been delivered by a 5-basis-point breakeven decline while the real yield rose 1 basis point. Tuesday's 2.41% real yield remained 23 basis points above its level 1 month earlier, but its daily decline showed that investors reduced the real compensation required for policy uncertainty and duration rather than treating cheaper oil solely as a mechanical headline-inflation adjustment.

The commodity move supported that shift without fully normalizing the inflation backdrop. Brent closed at $86.93, down 4.48% over 1 week, and WTI finished at $82.24, down 3.14% over the same period. Both contracts remained roughly 19% to 21% higher over 1 month. The immediate energy impulse weakened as diplomacy reduced the probability of another supply interruption, yet the accumulated monthly rise still left businesses and policymakers exposed to higher fuel and freight costs than before the conflict escalation. That tension explains why breakevens eased only marginally on Tuesday even as real yields rallied.

Fed pricing remained unusually resistant to the oil decline. At 3:30 p.m. New York time, swaps implied roughly a 1-in-3 probability of a 25-basis-point increase at the next day's decision, and markets still fully priced a quarter-point rise by September and nearly 50 basis points by March. Most economists expected no change, but Citadel Securities shifted its base case to a hike, and PGIM also judged the market to be underpricing that outcome. The distribution was wide because the debate concerned both the policy rate and whether Warsh would use an untelegraphed move to establish a less predictable reaction function.

Futures positioning made the event premium observable rather than rhetorical. Open interest in the August federal funds contract rose from 909,714 on Friday to 967,136 on Monday, exceeding the previous record associated with the October 2024 contract. The position build isolated the immediate hold-or-hike decision, while options activity also accumulated around later 2026 SOFR strikes. Treasury futures hedging remained more expensive against a long-bond selloff than against gains, showing that investors still regarded long-duration losses as the more costly tail even as spot yields declined.

Reduced guidance increases the amount of compensation required between meetings. Warsh has formed a task force to review Fed communications and has questioned the practice of repeatedly signaling the central bank's likely path. The approach may eventually reduce false precision, but ahead of July 29 it removed the usual anchor that keeps the expected decision within a few basis points of the eventual outcome. Since 2015, the average day-before error had been only 2.4 basis points. A meeting carrying roughly 8 basis points of expected tightening was therefore a material departure from recent operating convention.

The curve conclusion is narrower than the 3-day rally suggests. Lower oil produced a real-yield decline and a small bull-steepening, evidence that the energy shock was no longer tightening financial conditions through every rates channel. Yet the 1-month rise across the curve, a 30-year yield above 5%, and costly protection against a long-end selloff preserved the structural burden. Tuesday reduced the price of the immediate inflation tail; it did not settle whether the Fed path or the fiscal term premium can move sustainably lower.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit participated in the Treasury rally without signaling a large repricing of default risk. LQD rose 0.30%, while HYG gained 0.19% and JNK advanced 0.16%. The larger investment-grade move was consistent with its greater duration exposure, and the similar gains in the 2 high-yield funds indicated that risk appetite remained intact despite the semiconductor selloff. Over 1 month, however, LQD was still down 2.44%, compared with declines of 0.51% in HYG and 0.63% in JNK. High real yields, rather than broad credit stress, remained the larger aggregate drag.

The Meta-linked data-center financing showed how substantial concession can restore secondary demand. BlackRock sold $12.5 billion of bonds at a 7.53% yield and a 287.5-basis-point spread over Treasuries. Orders peaked at $20 billion, only 1.6 times the sale and far below the roughly 4-times average for US investment-grade offerings in 2026. The syndication took almost 1 week and did not tighten from initial discussions, while the final spread was the widest for an A-rated or higher bond in 3 years. Those terms located the absorption constraint in price, not in a closed market.

Secondary trading improved the verdict without erasing the initial signal. The spread tightened to about 267 basis points on Tuesday as the high yield attracted buyers. Meta is the initial sole tenant of the 1-gigawatt Texas facility, which is expected to begin operating in 2028; BlackRock funds own 80% of the venture and Meta retains 20%. Leases have a 4-year initial term and 4 extension options, and a residual-value guarantee covers certain shortfalls between the facility's fair value and a pre-agreed threshold. Investors were paid heavily even with a defined lease and asset-value support package.

AI credit risk is also migrating through guarantees and customer financing rather than only through conventional bond issuance. Nvidia's default-protection cost recorded its largest increase since active trading began as investors assessed more than $750 billion of infrastructure arrangements. Chinese progress in immersion deep-ultraviolet lithography added an operating threat at the same time, raising the possibility that financed capacity faces weaker pricing power. The credit question is no longer simply how much technology debt will be issued; it is which corporate balance sheets absorb lease, purchase and residual-value obligations if expected AI utilization disappoints.

Conventional acquisition finance remained available on materially simpler terms. Brady sold $800 million of privately placed, investment-grade debt to fund its $1.4 billion purchase of Honeywell's productivity-solutions business. The bonds spanned 5 to 10 years, with the largest $300 million 7-year tranche priced 125 basis points over the comparable Treasury. Brady also had a $1 billion term loan syndicated among lenders. The transaction shows that established cash-generating assets could still access multiple funding channels at a fraction of the Sopaipilla spread, preserving a clear distinction between ordinary M&A leverage and AI project concentration.

Tullow Oil illustrated how a commodity windfall can reopen a refinancing path that was previously unavailable. After extending roughly $1.2 billion of bonds in April, replacing a $400 million Glencore loan with $423 million of notes and adding a cargo-prepayment facility, the company was exploring cheaper debt for 2027. The reworked bonds traded near 102 cents, supported by stronger cash flow and an April cargo realized at $130 a barrel. Yet a springing maturity accelerates repayment by 6 months unless a sale agreement is signed by September 30, 2027, leaving execution tied to both operating progress and the oil price.

The non-rated municipal market presented a more aggressive transfer of operating risk. QCF/I planned to finance the purchase of Advantage Behavioral Health with about $610 million of bonds maturing in 2046 and 2057, marketed roughly 300 basis points above comparable AAA debt. About $415 million would go to Clearview Capital and company insiders, with another $100 million contingent on performance. Only $14.4 million of the business's value consisted of owned real estate, so bondholders were principally exposed to forecast operating cash flow rather than hard assets. A pipeline of about $3 billion of similar structures makes the precedent broader than a single sale.

European bank capital showed the opposite problem: abundant demand had compressed compensation before a loss event. A multicurrency AT1 index reached a record-tight spread of 211.3 basis points, and 2 banks priced preferred securities at their lowest reset spreads on record. The income remained attractive, but Man Group argued that investors were underweighting extension, coupon-cancellation and principal-loss risk in the most junior part of a bank's debt stack. US software refinancing supplied another scale test. Veritas-backed Gainwell was discussing replacement of almost $5.7 billion of debt, including about $4.2 billion of 1st-lien and $1.5 billion of 2nd-lien loans, as the software sector faced roughly $92 billion of leveraged-loan maturities by 2028. A bond-and-loan solution could extend the senior debt, while existing lenders might retain the junior piece; successful execution would therefore test both market capacity and how much risk remains with incumbent creditors. Credit liquidity was therefore functional but sharply segmented. Treasury gains supported total returns, the Meta-linked bonds found a secondary bid, and Brady funded an acquisition through private placements and bank debt. The market demanded much stronger compensation where repayment depended on long-horizon AI use, contingent guarantees, a commodity recovery or aggressive operating forecasts, while tight AT1 spreads showed that other complex risks were receiving unusually little compensation. Tuesday did not show a financing stop. It showed that structural protection, asset quality and concession were carrying more analytical weight than a broad risk-on label.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

European duration retained a structural steepening bias even as lower oil offered near-term relief. The euro 10s30s swap spread steepened for a 3rd session but remained near 10 basis points after the February conflict erased about 60% of the prior move. Investors still expected shorter maturities to outperform as fiscal issuance rises and the Netherlands shifts a €1.6 trillion pension system toward defined contribution. Markets priced 42 basis points of ECB increases by year-end. The front end remained hostage to energy and policy, while the long end faced a slower erosion of captive demand.

Japan carried the same tension through fiscal credibility and the currency. Reports that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi could direct officials to prepare a 2-year cut in the food consumption tax to 1% raised concern about financing and additional JGB issuance. The yen remained weaker than 163 per dollar, and the curve had flattened as shorter yields rose on expectations that the BOJ could tighten faster to contain imported inflation. Fiscal easing threatens the long end, whereas a faster policy path pressures the front end and reduces the relative attraction of foreign duration to Japanese buyers.

Market pricing reflected the difficulty of resolving both channels at once. Overnight swaps assigned about a 29% probability to a BOJ increase by September and 78% by October, even though 50% of surveyed economists expected the next move only in December. A 1% policy rate remained well below officials' discussion of a neutral rate near 2%. Taiwan reinforced the regional repricing: its 5-year yield jumped 16 basis points to 1.82%, the highest since November 2008, after a weak 20-year sale and expectations of at least 1 12.5-basis-point central-bank increase over 12 months.

After the US close, Chile's central bank held its policy rate at 4.5% for a 5th meeting in a unanimous decision. Brent had fallen below $85 during Tuesday after briefly trading above $100 the prior week, whipsawing inflation expectations in an economy that imports nearly all its fuel. The decline in oil was not enough to restart easing: June inflation had accelerated to 4.3% against a 3% target, while investment, consumption and employment indicators weakened. The decision captured the wider global constraint, in which cheaper spot energy reduces urgency but does not remove accumulated price pressure.

A later UK fiscal assessment preserved another source of long-duration competition. NIESR estimated that inflation and energy costs could erode £24 billion of public-service spending power during the current parliamentary term and remove about £3 billion of fiscal-rule headroom. It projected inflation averaging 3.1% in both 2026 and 2027, above the 2.4% average forecast by the IMF and OECD and close to the BOE's 3% middle scenario. NIESR expected the policy rate to remain at 3.75%, whereas markets priced at least 2 increases to 4.25%, leaving a consequential disagreement over the inflation path.

The UK buyer base was already responding to that uncertainty. Multi-asset funds increased bonds overall but cut gilts from 25% to 15% of their fixed-income allocations between December and June, redirecting exposure toward Germany, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and Canada. The shift involved a smaller pool than dedicated gilt funds, yet it showed that high nominal yield alone was not enough when inflation and domestic political risk reduced conviction. NIESR quantified the fiscal counterpart: higher energy prices, inflation and borrowing costs could remove £24 billion from public-service budgets during the parliamentary term and about £3 billion of headroom under the fiscal rules, even as inflation was projected to average 3.1% in both 2026 and 2027. It expected the BOE to hold at 3.75%, versus market pricing for 4.25%, because more borrowing to fill the gap would worsen an already unsustainable debt path. The global implication for Treasuries is a persistent competition for duration even when US yields rally. European pension reform and fiscal supply support steeper long curves; Japanese tax plans and a weak yen pull policy and issuance in opposite directions; Taiwan shows how quickly local liquidity withdrawal can reprice a previously low-yield market. Chile and the UK add evidence that an oil retreat does not automatically reopen easing space. Foreign sovereign yields and domestic funding needs therefore continue to limit the buyer response to lower US rates.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market dollar debt benefited from the US rally without receiving a strong currency tailwind. EMB rose 0.24%, and the long-duration EM dollar sovereign index gained 0.24%, while the Dollar Index slipped only 0.04% to 101.43. EM currencies finished roughly unchanged as oil importers gained and commodity exporters faced the opposite terms-of-trade impulse. The 3.7% fall in EM equities was dominated by Asian technology rather than a generalized dollar shortage. Lower Treasury real yields eased the common funding hurdle, but local balance sheets determined the distribution.

UAE issuance demonstrated resilience under direct geopolitical pressure. Sovereigns and companies raised $30.3 billion in dollar and euro bonds through July 28, 33% more than a year earlier and $3.7 billion above the previous record for the period. Recent sales included $600 million from RAK Bank, $500 million from Burjeel and a $300 million Ajman sukuk; most were oversubscribed and tightened from initial guidance. UAE sovereign dollar bonds still traded about 77 basis points over Treasuries, wider than 65 before the war, showing that market access and a larger conflict premium could coexist.

That access was not uniform across debt-management strategies. Colombia's comptroller challenged an October exchange of 43.4 trillion pesos of TES for 35.4 trillion pesos of new securities, which reduced nominal debt by about 8 trillion pesos and extended maturities. The new bonds carried 11.75% and 12% coupons instead of roughly 7.25%, increasing annual interest expense by about 316.5 billion pesos. The Finance Ministry argued that lower coupons would have required deeper discounts and more nominal issuance, but the referral for disciplinary review introduced legal and institutional risk into future liability management.

The Colombian case matters beyond the accounting dispute because it separates near-term liquidity relief from intertemporal fiscal capacity. A 3.5%-of-GDP primary deficit in 2025 had already weakened the setting in which the exchange occurred. Replacing short instruments with expensive long bonds reduced rollover pressure, yet it also committed future administrations to higher debt service and reduced room for other spending. For sovereign investors, maturity extension cannot be treated as an unqualified improvement when the coupon burden and governance process change at the same time.

Primary access elsewhere remained selective. Uruguay moved to reopen local-currency bonds due in 2035 and dollar bonds due in 2037, while the broader EM currency index absorbed the oil decline with little net change. The oil shock redistributed rather than uniformly tightened conditions: importers such as Chile received currency relief, whereas energy-linked borrowers lost part of a recent revenue tailwind. A stable dollar and lower US real yields improved the external setting, but neither could neutralize fiscal execution, commodity sensitivity or the legal durability of debt-management choices.

The EM conclusion was relief in the common factor with persistent sovereign dispersion. Hard-currency duration gained, Gulf issuers retained market access, and there was no broad dollar-liquidity break. Wider UAE spreads and Colombia's contested exchange showed where risk remained embedded: geopolitical exposure was being priced even when orderbooks held, and maturity management was being judged against its full future cost. The US rally improved the discount rate; it did not homogenize sovereign credit quality.

## Cross asset

Cross assets confirmed the rates rally's oil origin but rejected a broad recession or liquidation reading. Brent fell 1.62% to $86.93 and WTI declined 0.45% to $82.24, extending the de-escalation move that lowered nominal and real Treasury yields. The S&P 500 nevertheless gained 0.21%, and the equal-weighted index reached a record as defensive and non-technology shares offset weakness in former AI leaders. The VIX fell 2.46% to 18.21. Lower yields were compatible with continued broad equity resilience.

The contradiction was concentrated in technology. The Nasdaq 100 lost 0.98%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 4.49%, and the latter's declines reached 10.69% over 1 week and 16.42% over 1 month. Asian semiconductor shares also suffered severe losses as investors combined Chinese capacity risk with concern about circular AI funding. This dispersion strengthens the credit interpretation: the market was questioning the returns and obligation structure of a capital-intensive sector, not pricing an economy-wide collapse in cash flow.

The dollar and gold further limited a haven explanation. The Dollar Index was almost unchanged, and gold futures fell 1.25% to $4,023.40 even as Treasuries gained. Credit funds and EM debt also advanced. The combined pattern points to lower energy inflation and reduced real-rate pressure as the principal easing channels, with sector-specific technology stress operating alongside them. It does not resemble indiscriminate demand for liquidity or a generalized retreat from credit risk.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 29 FOMC decision determines whether the decline in real yields can survive the removal of event risk. A 25-basis-point increase, or a hold that preserves near-term tightening as an active option, keeps the relevant pressure in the 2-year yield, federal funds futures and the real component of intermediate Treasuries; a patient hold that gives greater weight to lower oil and June's softer inflation requires those measures to extend their rally rather than relying on another fall in breakevens. The July 31 Employment Cost Index then tests whether wage pressure supports the Fed's residual inflation concern after the energy impulse eased. A renewed rise in Brent toward the prior week's highs would reopen both channels and make Tuesday's bull-steepening look provisional.

Microsoft and Meta results on July 29, followed by Apple and Amazon on July 30, provide the cash-flow and obligation test for AI credit. Durable revenue against disclosed capital commitments, limited new guarantees and a Sopaipilla spread holding near or inside Tuesday's 267-basis-point level would preserve the interpretation that its 7.53% yield was a large but effective clearing concession. Higher spending without commensurate cash generation, additional customer-financing commitments or renewed weakness in Nvidia default protection would broaden the concern from semiconductor equities to high-grade balance sheets. The sensitive channels are long-dated technology bonds, subsequent orderbooks and the pricing of project structures that rely on leases and residual-value support.

The Bank of England decision on July 30 and the Bank of Japan decision on July 31 test whether foreign curves release any of the pressure competing with Treasuries. UK guidance validating the market's path toward 4.25% would reinforce the inflation and fiscal premium in gilts, whereas a 3.75%-centered outlook closer to NIESR's view requires lower yields and steadier inflation expectations to be credible. In Japan, guidance bringing a hike closer than December must stabilize the yen without producing another front-end selloff; a dovish message risks a move beyond 165 per dollar and renewed intervention concern. The net Treasury consequence depends on whether these outcomes lower foreign sovereign yields and improve hedged demand for US duration, or keep domestic assets competitive for global balance sheets.
